name: lemlist
summary: Lemlist’s public API authenticates with account-scoped API keys over HTTP Basic auth (no third‑party OAuth client registration). If you’re building an agent, plan to collect one API key per customer account, store it securely, and call REST endpoints directly. Lemlist hosts its own OAuth for its MCP (LLM connector) and CLI, but this does not require or allow developers to register client apps with Lemlist.

composio.note: Bring your own OAuth app; register the redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Note: Lemlist’s REST API uses API keys, not OAuth; for MCP connections Lemlist hosts its own OAuth and does not expose third‑party client registration.

verdict.difficultyReason: No OAuth app or consent screen to configure; you only generate an API key and call REST endpoints. Webhooks and rate limits are documented.
verdict.timeToFirstToken: ~10 minutes with an API key; no OAuth client needed.

prerequisites.text: A Lemlist account with access to Settings → Integrations → API & Webhooks.
Team role that can generate API keys (admin or a role with API access and Edit integrations).
Server or vault to store API keys (secret manager, KMS, or environment variables).

steps.title: Generate a Lemlist API key
steps.detail: Sign in to app.lemlist.com → click your avatar (bottom-left) → Settings → Integrations → API & Webhooks → Generate a new API key. Copy it once and store securely.
tips: The username is blank and the password is your API key in Basic auth.

steps.title: Store the key securely
steps.detail: Place the key in your secrets manager or encrypted environment variables. Rotate if exposed. Keep one key per customer account.
tips: Treat like a password; never commit to git.
Document where each key is used.

steps.title: Implement HTTP Basic authentication
steps.detail: Build the string ":API_KEY" (note the leading colon), Base64‑encode it, and send Authorization: Basic <encoded>. Example curl: curl --location 'https://api.lemlist.com/api/{endpoint}' --header 'Authorization: Basic BASE64(:API_KEY)'.
tips: Do not send Bearer tokens; Lemlist uses Basic auth.
Most HTTP clients can set --user ":API_KEY" to build the header.

steps.title: Select and test endpoints you need
steps.detail: Start with read-only (e.g., GET /campaigns, GET /leads by email), then implement writes like POST /campaigns/{id}/leads. Verify 2xx/4xx handling and idempotency where relevant.
tips: Use the API reference examples to shape request bodies.
Capture error payloads for support and retries.

steps.title: Build retry/backoff for rate limits
steps.detail: Respect 20 requests per 2 seconds per key. On 429, read Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset and back off accordingly.

steps.title: Configure webhooks (optional)
steps.detail: Create webhooks for events you track (e.g., interested replies, campaign events). The API key’s user must have the Edit integrations permission, otherwise requests fail with 403.
tips: Validate signatures if provided; log deliveries.
Use a unique webhook per environment.

steps.title: Support multiple customer accounts
steps.detail: Each API key maps to one Lemlist account. Store one credential per account and switch keys to act on different customers.
tips: No account parameter; the key selects the account.

steps.title: Limit blast radius and rotate keys
steps.detail: Issue distinct keys per environment and per integration, audit usage, and rotate on staff changes or suspected exposure.

steps.title: Verify plan/permissions for the features you call
steps.detail: If an endpoint returns 403, confirm the team role and plan allow the action (admin or custom role with API access). Adjust role permissions or contact Lemlist support if needed.

steps.title: Optional: connect via Lemlist’s hosted MCP OAuth
steps.detail: If your agent platform supports MCP, point it to https://app.lemlist.com/mcp and complete user authorization. This flow is hosted by Lemlist; you do not register an OAuth client.
tips: Prefer API keys for backend integrations you control.
Use OAuth in end-user LLM clients that manage tokens for you.

scopes.note: No third‑party OAuth scopes: Lemlist’s REST API uses API keys over HTTP Basic auth. Lemlist-hosted OAuth for MCP/CLI is first‑party and does not require developer app registration.

approval.process: No app review or publishing process for REST API usage; you generate a key per account and can use it immediately.

nuances.title: HTTP Basic, not Bearer
nuances.detail: All REST calls use Authorization: Basic with base64(":API_KEY"). Bearer tokens will fail.

nuances.title: Per‑account credentials
nuances.detail: Each API key (or Lemlist‑hosted OAuth token) maps to a single Lemlist account. Switching accounts = switching keys.

nuances.title: Edit integrations permission for webhooks
nuances.detail: Webhook writes fail with 403 unless the API key’s user has Edit integrations.

nuances.title: Rate limit is 20 requests / 2 seconds
nuances.detail: Enforce client-side throttling and exponential backoff; read Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers.

nuances.title: Secrets visible once
nuances.detail: You can only view an API key at creation—store it securely; otherwise, rotate and reissue.

nuances.title: No third‑party OAuth client registration
nuances.detail: Lemlist does not expose a console to register external OAuth apps; use API keys or Lemlist’s hosted OAuth for MCP.

blockers.blocker: Need one key per customer account; cannot impersonate multiple accounts with one credential.
blockers.workaround: Collect and store a separate API key per tenant; route requests by tenant key.

blockers.blocker: 403 on webhook creation due to insufficient rights.
blockers.workaround: Have an admin (or a role with Edit integrations) generate the key or grant the permission; retry.

blockers.blocker: Hitting global rate limits under batch imports/syncs.
blockers.workaround: Queue and throttle to ≤20 req/2s per key; use backoff on 429 and parallelize across tenants with distinct keys.

blockers.blocker: Expecting OAuth scopes/refresh tokens for REST API.
blockers.workaround: Use API keys for server-to-server; if you need user-consented flows inside LLM clients, use Lemlist’s hosted MCP OAuth instead.

agentDoes: Drafts integration plan and endpoint list from the API reference.
Generates webhook payload handlers and test calls.
Prepares per-tenant credential storage and rotation scripts.
Runs smoke tests against read and write endpoints.
humanDoes: Log in and generate API keys for each Lemlist account.
Grant required team permissions (e.g., Edit integrations) where needed.
Approve optional MCP OAuth consent when connecting from an LLM client.
Decide on plan level or contact Lemlist support if an endpoint appears permission-gated.
